response:
It is completely okay that you don't feel a strong emotional reaction to your parents' divorce. Everyone processes big family changes differently, and feeling indifferent is a valid response. It makes sense that you find it frustrating to be pushed into counseling when they are the ones still arguing.

If you decide to go just to keep the peace, remember that therapy doesn't have to be about the divorce. You could use that time to talk about how stressful their fighting is, or just focus on your own life, school, and goals. However, if you really don't want to go, having an honest conversation might be better than using homework as an excuse. You could calmly explain that you have already processed your feelings, but that their ongoing arguments are what actually bothers you. Ultimately, counseling works best when you want to be there, but it could also just serve as a private space to vent about their behavior.
